## Request Context
- **What was requested**: Review Pattern 1 of the D2 backflow harvest (SPEC-20260610-205507): the one-shot-stop-hook port from dan_research_karpathy_wiki, reviewed ALONE per the SPEC (highest blast radius of the 5 patterns - touches Stop-hook wiring). Overnight mission Run 2, autonomous authorization active.
- **Files/scope**: scripts/stop_hook.py (NEW), scripts/queue_stop_notify.py (NEW), tests/test_stop_hook.py (NEW, 18 tests), docs/adr/ADR-0023-one-shot-stop-hook.md (NEW), docs/drafts/DRAFT-20260612-settings-stop-hook.diff (NEW, parked - developer applies settings.json manually)
- **Developer-stated motivation**: Back-flow obligation recorded in the wiki's framework-lineage.yaml ledger (owed -> delivered); template has no Stop hook at all; autonomous sessions end silently.
- **Explicit constraints**: NEVER edit .claude/settings.json (draft diff only); untrusted-reply allow-list invariant is non-negotiable (act on matched label only, never raw text); no-slug + ASCII console invariants from the regression ledger; single-poller lockfile discipline (2026-06-07 misfiling bug class).

Verdict: approve-with-changes. Adversarial review of the new ntfy-reply trust boundary. NO critical/high findings - the allow-list-only injection control holds (raw reply never printed/injected, proven by tests).
1. Severity: medium - slug-as-auth residual: an attacker with the topic slug can forge an allow-listed choice during the wait window (one-tap gated-action forgery); not new vs collab_loop (same auth model), blast radius bounded to pre-declared labels. ADR should document the residual + mitigations (non-obvious labels for destructive actions, short wait windows). Rule: an allow-list must not create a false sense of authentication when the channel auth is a bearer-equivalent secret.
2. Severity: medium - fetch_reply has no allow-list at its own layer; stop_hook is the sole enforcement point (match_choice at the caller). A refactor interpolating reply instead of label would silently regress. Mitigant: hook-layer tests exist. Recommend: ADR states fetch_reply is the deliberately-unsafe primitive + every result MUST wrap match_choice; add a superset-reply test (choice Go, reply 'Go ahead and rm -rf') pinning no injection.
3. Severity: low - match_choice casefold exact-match is correct; avoid casefold-colliding labels (Kelvin-sign class). No change.
4. Severity: low - draft timeout 630 vs cap 600: margin must absorb send (10s) + final poll HTTP (15s) + spawn; thin. Widen to 660 or document the margin budget.
5. Severity: low - matcher '' means FIRST stop after queuing consumes the one-shot (incl. subagent stops). Intent-file writers are same-authority (no escalation); document the ordering contract.
6. Severity: low - DoS surface verified bounded: every malformed/no-topic path deletes the intent; no wedge possible. Strength, not a defect.
Trust boundaries verified clean: no str(exc)/URL/slug on any error path; ASCII throughout. Strengths: fail-closed posture consistent + tested; single-poller stand-down within one cycle; settings change correctly parked as draft.

Verdict: approve-with-changes. 18 tests pin the critical security invariants well (allow-list, single-poller, no-slug, ASCII, fail-closed); state-machine edges are thinner.
1. Severity: high - priority value-set mismatch: queue CLI accepts 'urgent' but notify.py's documented set is min/low/default/high/max; intent passes through unvalidated. ntfy accepts urgent as a max alias so no crash; silent inconsistency + zero priority tests. Fix: align the queue CLI choices to notify's set + parametrized pass-through test.
2. Severity: high - non-list choices degradation: intent '"choices": "Approve"' (hand-written JSON) iterates CHARACTERS - allow-list silently becomes single letters; reply 'a' would match and inject 'A'. Security-relevant integrity failure of the allow-list. Fix: isinstance(choices, list) guard failing closed + test.
3. Severity: medium - garbage wait_timeout_seconds ('abc') silently falls back to 120s polling; untested. Pin with a test or validate.
4. Severity: medium - TOCTOU between exists() and read_text: handled correctly via OSError catch (verified), but unpinned; add FileNotFoundError race test.
5. Severity: medium - REVIEW.md rule 15: tags argument never asserted (incl. ''->None coercion path). Add assertions.
6. Severity: medium - queue CLI mkdir(parents=True) path untested with missing parent chain.
7. Severity: medium - superseded-lock test lacks @pytest.mark.regression linking the 2026-06-07 misfiling ledger class.
8. Severity: low - duplicate/empty choices untested (filter exists for empties; dups benign).
9. Severity: low - queue CLI print of non-ASCII title could UnicodeEncodeError on cp1252 (4th-occurrence class); sanitize or accept documented risk.
Strengths: correct mock seams (module attributes); deterministic clock manipulation; claimed-args asserted not just counts; slug-in-exception test is a true invariant pin; cross-module cap-consistency test.

Verdict: approve-with-changes (Independent Analyst). Overlap question answered: NOT ceremony - the genuine new capability is firing on ABNORMAL session end (crash/kill), which collab_loop.say-from-the-orchestrator cannot do; the --wait sub-path is the optional/most-complex part.
1. Severity: medium - the --wait path uses ask_developer.fetch_reply (the legacy shim whose own docstring says it has NO in-code allow-list) with caller-side match_choice, re-introducing the caller-enforcement pattern ADR-0019 R3 rejected in favor of boundary enforcement. Holds today; refactor-fragile over 6-12 months. Decision needed: accept frozen-shim status (documented) or route through collab_loop's enforcing seams.
2. Severity: low - the Stop-hook 'decision: block' harness contract is assumed, never cited; add a citation/comment (wiki deployment = empirical evidence).
3. Severity: low - STOP_HOOK_DISABLE preserves intent by design = stale-intent footgun (developer forgets the env var; a later unrelated session fires an old gated question). Suggest timestamp TTL guard (~4h) per Principle 8.
4. Severity: low - WAIT_TIMEOUT_CAP duplicated across two files; guarded by a cross-module test; acceptable for standalone-script portability. Accepted trade-off.
Pre-mortems: stale-intent firing (medium likelihood w/ DISABLE); lock supersession orphaning a reply (low, inherent to shared-lock architecture, stands down cleanly); concurrent queue = single-slot mailbox overwrite (low; document).
What I'd have done differently (advisory): ship notify-only first, add --wait after empirically confirming the harness contract. Strengths: silent-by-default correct + credited to wiki iteration history; uninstalled-topic path cleanly handled; draft-diff governance correct.

Finding verification: 11 verified, 6 inconclusive (judgment-dependent design/doc advisories), 0 discarded. Key verifications by direct code read: qa#2 non-list choices char-degradation CONFIRMED (intent.get('choices') or [] iterates a string); qa#1 priority set mismatch CONFIRMED (queue CLI 'urgent' vs notify.py documented 'max'; pass-through header, ntfy tolerates - severity recalibrated high->medium); sec#4 timeout margin CONFIRMED thin (600 cap + 15s POLL_HTTP_TIMEOUT vs 630); qa#4 TOCTOU CONFIRMED already-handled (OSError catch covers FileNotFoundError); indep#1 fetch_reply caller-enforcement CONFIRMED by docstring. FOLDED in-session: (1) isinstance(choices,list) fail-closed guard + test; (2) priority choices aligned to notify's set + parametrized pass-through test; (3) superset-reply pin test (choice Go vs 'Go ahead and rm -rf'); (4) tags assertions incl. ''->None; (5) @pytest.mark.regression on superseded-lock test; (6) intent TTL 4h via queued_at stamp + 2 tests (stale discarded / fresh fires); (7) draft timeout 630->660 + margin budget documented; (8) ADR residual-risks section (slug-forgery window, fetch_reply unsafe-primitive contract, first-stop-wins ordering) + stop-hook decision:block contract citation comment. Tests 18->28, all pass. NOT folded (accepted/advisory): garbage-timeout fallback test, mkdir-chain test, duplicate-choices test, WAIT_TIMEOUT_CAP duplication (guarded by cross-module test), notify-only-first sequencing observation.

## Request Context
- What was requested: Review Pattern 1 of the D2 backflow harvest (SPEC-20260610-205507): one-shot-stop-hook port from dan_research_karpathy_wiki, reviewed ALONE (highest blast radius of the 5 owed patterns - Stop-hook wiring + a new untrusted-input boundary). Overnight Run 2, autonomous authorization.
- Files/scope: scripts/stop_hook.py, scripts/queue_stop_notify.py, tests/test_stop_hook.py (28 tests post-fold), docs/adr/ADR-0023-one-shot-stop-hook.md, docs/drafts/DRAFT-20260612-settings-stop-hook.diff (parked).
- Developer-stated motivation: wiki back-flow ledger obligation; template has no Stop hook; autonomous sessions end silently.
- Explicit constraints: settings.json never agent-edited (draft parked); untrusted-reply allow-list invariant; no-slug + ASCII invariants; single-poller discipline.

## Verdict: APPROVE (post-fold)
Panel: security-specialist (opus, adversarial) 0.86 approve-with-changes; qa-specialist (sonnet) 0.87 approve-with-changes; independent-perspective (sonnet, Independent Analyst) 0.82 approve-with-changes. Facilitator verification: 11 verified, 6 inconclusive, 0 discarded.
ZERO critical findings. The core security control - allow-list-only injection of the canonical label, raw reply never printed or injected - HOLDS, adversarially probed and pinned by tests (incl. new superset-reply pin). The one security-relevant defect (non-list choices degrading the allow-list to characters) was folded with a fail-closed guard + test. All 8 actionable folds applied in-session; tests 18->28 green.
Blocking findings: 1 (qa#2 choices degradation) - FIXED in-session. Advisory: 10 (3 folded as code, 4 folded as docs/ADR, 3 accepted with rationale). Speculative (<0.80 confidence): 0. Unscored: 0.
Independent-perspective frame answer: the port is NOT ceremony - firing on abnormal session end is a genuine capability collab_loop.say cannot provide; the --wait path is the optional complexity and its assumptions are now documented + tested.
Model tiers: security-specialist:opus, qa-specialist:sonnet, independent-perspective:sonnet, facilitator:main-loop (lean-dispatch policy).
Education gate: recommended at Bloom's Understand/Apply for the developer cohort (deferred per auth E - overnight): the intent-file schema, the allow-list injection contract, and when to use queue_stop_notify vs collab_loop ask.

## What I Missed
The non-list choices guard - a real input-validation gap squarely in my domain (caller passing a bare string/None upstream of the enforce point); I traced the happy path through fetch_reply but did not enumerate malformed-caller inputs. Also did not explicitly verify the superset-reply pin.
## Candidate Improvement Rule
For every allow-list enforcement function, enumerate the three degenerate caller inputs (None, wrong type, empty collection) and verify fail-closed behavior for each before marking the boundary clean.
## Confidence Calibration
Original: 0.86, Revised: 0.79, Delta: -0.07

## What I Missed
I rated the priority mismatch High while my own Exceptions clause described the actual runtime behavior (ntfy tolerates urgent) - apply the exception BEFORE assigning severity, not after.
## Candidate Improvement Rule
Exception-First Severity Rule: before assigning severity to an assertion-correctness finding, evaluate whether the finding's own exception clause is satisfied by observable runtime behavior; if so, cap at Medium and note it.
## Confidence Calibration
Original: 0.87, Revised: 0.82, Delta: -0.05

## What I Missed
The failure-of-the-hook-itself path: a silently dropped notification (network down) leaves no signal an abnormal stop occurred; and whether the hook covers the supervisor-orphan scenario (feedback_supervisor_taskstop_orphans_child).
## Candidate Improvement Rule
For any hook that fires on failure paths, explicitly trace the hook's own failure path; require a local fallback signal or documented acceptance of silent drop.
## Confidence Calibration
Original: 0.82, Revised: 0.76, Delta: -0.06
